In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the refrigeration load for the oil entrainment in a vertical section of a refrigerant line is a strong function of the refrigerant mass flow rate, the inner radius of the riser, and the viscosity of the lubricating oil.

the oil entrainment problem in vertical refrigerant lines is a complex problem and the solution of which is not possible without considering the effect of the oil viscosity, surface tension, and the refrigerant viscosity and the effect of the refrigerant pressure and temperature.

the minimum refrigeration load for carrying the oil up in a vertical section of refrigerant piping is dependent upon the pipe material, pipe diameter and length, oil viscosity, oil density and the refrigerant mass flow rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a minimum capacity of about 0.5 kW is required to carry the oil up in vertical risers.
the required minimum refrigeration capacity for carrying the lubricant up a vertical section of the refrigerant line is a linear function of the refrigerant velocity.
the required refrigeration load for oil entrainment is very small and can be neglected for practical purposes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the refrigerant velocity required to carry oil up in the vertical suction riser of a refrigeration system is not as large as commonly believed.
the oil return velocity is proportional to the refrigeration capacity and the riser length.

the refrigerant speed for oil entrainment in vertical sections is not a constant value, as is often assumed, but rather a variable function of the oil film thickness and the vapor velocity, both of which vary with the refrigerant mass flow rate.
